author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed, with one correction to the sizing.

AiaConfig gained max_response_bytes, default AIA_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES, enforced in parse_ca_issuers_response before any parsing. That function is the chokepoint for both the single-certificate and the certs-only CMS paths, which is a better site than build_with_aia -- the suggested one -- because build_with_aia no longer decodes anything directly; it delegates to the sans-I/O builder.

The correction: the bead sized the cap for ONE certificate (64 KiB, 'well under 32 KiB for a single cert, 16x headroom'). But this function also decodes certs-only CMS bundles of up to max_certs_per_response certificates, 16 by default, and a pathological certificate with many SANs reaches about 16 KiB. 16 x 16 KiB is 256 KiB, so a 64 KiB cap would have sat on top of legitimate traffic and rejected valid bundles. The default is 256 KiB, and a test asserts the default admits a full bundle at those limits so the two numbers cannot drift apart.

Reused AiaError::ResponseTooLarge { limit, actual } rather than adding a variant: it already exists with exactly the right shape and meaning, and is what pkix-aia-http reports for the same condition, so a caller handling one handles both.

Configurable rather than a private const, because every other AIA limit is. AiaConfig is #[non_exhaustive], so the field is additive.

pkix-chain 0.9.0, not a patch: a response over the cap now errors where it previously parsed, which is the same reasoning used for pkix-ct 0.4.0 today.

Mutation-verified.
